quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Mum made a shopping list before going out. She drove to the supermarket and put items in her trolley. She paid at the checkout and drove home.
options: Mum made a shopping list before going out.
She put items in her trolley at the supermarket.
She paid at the checkout and drove home.
Mum forgot the shopping list at home.
quests.hint: Look for the shopping sequence: preparing the list, filling the trolley, then paying. One frame contradicts the preparation step.
quests.explanation: Shopping narratives show preparation, selection, and payment as the three key stages.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The dog barked loudly at the front door. Tom went to see who was there. He opened the door and found a friend standing outside.
options: Tom ignored the barking and stayed asleep.
The dog barked loudly at the front door.
Tom went to see who was there.
Tom opened the door and found a friend.
quests.hint: Follow the sequence: the dog barks, Tom investigates, then opens the door. One frame shows the wrong response.
quests.explanation: Cause-and-effect narratives show a signal, an investigation, and a discovery. The distractor replaces action with inaction.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Ella set the oven to the right temperature. She placed the pizza on the baking tray and put it inside. After fifteen minutes, she took out the golden pizza.
options: Ella set the oven to the right temperature.
She placed the pizza in the oven.
Ella ordered a pizza for home delivery.
Ella took out the golden pizza after fifteen minutes.
quests.hint: Follow the cooking steps: preheating, placing, then removing. One frame skips the cooking process entirely.
quests.explanation: Cooking narratives follow preparation, cooking, and completion. The distractor replaces home cooking with a delivery order.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Leo felt cold and wrapped himself in a blanket. He made a hot cup of tea and sat by the fireplace. After an hour he felt much warmer.
options: Leo felt cold and wrapped himself in a blanket.
Leo went outside for a walk in the cold.
He made a hot cup of tea by the fireplace.
Leo felt much warmer after an hour.
quests.hint: Sequence the comfort story: feeling cold, warming up, then the result. One frame contradicts the cosy setting.
quests.explanation: Comfort narratives move from discomfort to action to relief. The distractor replaces warmth-seeking with exposure to the cold.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Nina woke up feeling unwell. She told her mum, who took her temperature. Her mum gave her some medicine and told her to rest in bed.
options: Nina woke up feeling unwell.
Her mum took her temperature.
Nina's mum gave her medicine and told her to rest.
Nina went to school despite feeling unwell.
quests.hint: Follow the health sequence: feeling sick, being checked, then receiving care. One frame ignores the illness.
quests.explanation: Home healthcare stories show reporting, diagnosing, and treating as the three steps. The distractor bypasses care entirely.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: It was getting dark outside. Kim closed the curtains and switched on the living room lamp. She settled on the sofa with a book.
options: Kim went to bed immediately when it got dark.
It was getting dark outside.
Kim closed the curtains and switched on the lamp.
Kim settled on the sofa with a book.
quests.hint: Trace the evening routine: noticing the dark, preparing the room, then relaxing. One frame skips the relaxation step.
quests.explanation: Evening routine narratives follow: noticing dark, preparing comfort, and settling down. The distractor skips to bedtime too early.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Grandpa sat down in his garden and picked up his newspaper. He read the news stories slowly and carefully. After finishing, he fell asleep in his chair.
options: Grandpa sat down and picked up his newspaper.
He read the news stories slowly and carefully.
Grandpa threw away the newspaper unread.
Grandpa fell asleep in his chair after finishing.
quests.hint: Sequence the garden reading: sitting down, reading, then the result. One frame contradicts the whole activity.
quests.explanation: Relaxation narratives show settling, doing an activity, and the resulting calm. The distractor removes the activity entirely.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The park was full of fallen leaves. A group of children gathered them into a big pile. They took turns jumping into the pile with shouts of joy.
options: The park was full of fallen leaves.
The park gardener immediately swept the leaves away.
Children gathered the leaves into a big pile.
The children took turns jumping into the pile.
quests.hint: Follow the autumn play: noticing the leaves, gathering them, then playing. One frame introduces an adult who stops the fun.
quests.explanation: Play narratives show setting, preparation, and enjoyment. The distractor introduces an authority figure who prevents the play.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Mike noticed his bicycle tyre was flat. He found the puncture repair kit in the garage. He fixed the tyre and pumped it back up before school.
options: Mike noticed his bicycle tyre was flat.
He found the puncture repair kit in the garage.
Mike fixed the tyre and pumped it up before school.
Mike left his bicycle at home and walked to school.
quests.hint: Follow the problem-solving story: noticing, finding a solution, then fixing. One frame skips the repair entirely.
quests.explanation: Repair narratives show noticing a problem, locating the tools, and solving it. The distractor replaces fixing with avoidance.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The team meeting was scheduled for nine o'clock. Everyone arrived and sat around the table. The manager opened the meeting and shared the day's plan.
options: The meeting was postponed until the following week.
The team meeting was scheduled for nine o'clock.
Everyone arrived and sat around the table.
The manager opened the meeting and shared the plan.
quests.hint: Sequence the meeting story: the schedule, arrival, then the start. One frame postpones the event.
quests.explanation: Meeting narratives show scheduling, gathering, and starting. The distractor delays the event rather than letting it begin.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: It started raining heavily during the picnic. The family quickly packed up the food and blankets. They ran to the car and drove home laughing.
options: It started raining heavily during the picnic.
The family quickly packed up the food and blankets.
The family stayed outside and continued the picnic.
They ran to the car and drove home laughing.
quests.hint: Follow the rain story: the rain starts, the family packs up, then they leave. One frame ignores the rain entirely.
quests.explanation: Disruption narratives show an unexpected event, a response, and a resolution. The distractor pretends the disruption did not happen.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Oliver found a ten-pound note on the pavement. He looked around to see if anyone had dropped it. He handed it in at the nearby police station.
options: Oliver found a ten-pound note on the pavement.
Oliver put the money in his pocket and walked on.
He looked around to see if anyone had dropped it.
Oliver handed the note in at the police station.
quests.hint: Sequence the honest action: finding, checking, then handing in. One frame shows dishonesty instead.
quests.explanation: Honest-action narratives show discovery, consideration, and doing the right thing. The distractor replaces honesty with selfishness.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Sophie wanted to bake biscuits for her class. She followed the recipe step by step. The biscuits came out perfectly and everyone enjoyed them.
options: Sophie decided to bake biscuits for her class.
She followed the recipe step by step.
The biscuits came out perfectly and everyone enjoyed them.
Sophie forgot to bring the biscuits to school.
quests.hint: Trace the baking story: planning, following the recipe, then the outcome. One frame removes the successful delivery.
quests.explanation: Preparation-for-others narratives show intent, careful execution, and a shared reward. The distractor removes the sharing.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Harry planted a small oak tree in the garden. He watered it every day for a whole year. The little tree grew tall and strong by the following spring.
options: The oak tree was removed by the council.
Harry planted a small oak tree in the garden.
He watered it every day for a whole year.
The tree grew tall and strong by the following spring.
quests.hint: Follow the growth story: planting, consistent care, then the result. One frame replaces growth with removal.
quests.explanation: Nurturing narratives follow plant, tend, and grow. The distractor introduces an authority that removes the tree.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The kitchen was in a terrible mess after the party. The family worked together to wash the dishes and mop the floor. By bedtime, the kitchen was spotless.
options: The kitchen was a terrible mess after the party.
The family worked together to wash and mop.

By bedtime, the kitchen was spotless.

quests.explanation: Teamwork narratives show a problem, a shared response, and a clean result. The distractor replaces family cooperation with a hired service.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The village had no playground for the children. Local families wrote a letter to the council. The council approved the project and built a playground.
options: The village had no playground for children.
The council rejected the families' request.

The council approved and built a playground.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The car would not start on a cold winter morning. Dad called roadside assistance. The technician arrived and fixed the problem within twenty minutes.
options: The car would not start on a cold winter morning.
Dad called roadside assistance for help.

Dad sold the car and bought a new one.
quests.hint: Sequence the breakdown: the problem, calling help, then the fix. One frame gives an extreme response to a small problem.
quests.explanation: Breakdown narratives show a problem, a call for help, and a quick repair. The distractor replaces a simple fix with a drastic decision.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The children entered the library very quietly. They chose their books and found comfortable seats. They read in silence for the rest of the afternoon.
options: The children made so much noise that they were asked to leave.
The children entered the library very quietly.
They chose their books and found seats.
They read in silence for the afternoon.
quests.hint: Follow the library visit: entering quietly, selecting, then reading. One frame reverses the respectful behaviour.
quests.explanation: Respectful visit narratives show appropriate entry, selection, and quiet activity. The distractor introduces disruptive behaviour.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Maya received a birthday card in the post. She opened it and read the kind message inside. She called her friend to say thank you.
options: Maya received a birthday card in the post.
She opened it and read the kind message inside.
Maya threw the birthday card in the bin.
Maya called her friend to say thank you.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The old oak tree fell across the road in the storm. A local farmer came with a chainsaw to cut it up. By morning the road was clear again.
options: The old oak tree fell across the road in the storm.
The road stayed blocked for the entire week.
A local farmer came with a chainsaw to cut it up.
The road was clear again by morning.
quests.hint: Follow the storm story: the tree falls, a farmer clears it, then the road is open. One frame extends the blockage.
quests.explanation: Problem-resolution narratives show an event, a helper, and a successful outcome. The distractor replaces resolution with a prolonged problem.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The children set up a lemonade stand outside their house. They made fresh lemonade and wrote a price sign. By the afternoon they had sold every cup.
options: The children set up a lemonade stand outside.
They made fresh lemonade and wrote a price sign.

quests.explanation: Small business narratives show setup, production, and success. The distractor replaces a sold-out ending with no sales at all.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: Ava lost her phone at school. She asked her friends if anyone had seen it. Her teacher found it in the classroom and returned it to her.
options: Ava bought a brand-new phone to replace it.
Ava lost her phone at school.
She asked her friends if anyone had seen it.
Her teacher found the phone and returned it.

quests.explanation: Lost-and-found narratives progress from loss to search to recovery. The distractor bypasses the search and returns directly to replacement.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The young nurse arrived at the ward early for her shift. She checked each patient's notes carefully before starting her rounds. She gave everyone their morning medication on time.
options: The nurse arrived at the ward early for her shift.
She checked each patient's notes carefully.
The nurse arrived late and missed the morning rounds.
She gave everyone their morning medication on time.

quests.explanation: Professional duty narratives show punctuality, preparation, and careful execution. The distractor replaces dedication with tardiness.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
quests.story: The bakery ran out of bread early on Sunday morning. The baker made a new batch immediately. Fresh loaves were ready by ten o'clock.
options: The bakery ran out of bread early on Sunday.
The bakery closed for the rest of the day.

Fresh loaves were ready by ten o'clock.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.

The café was completely full by noon.

quests.instruction: Arrange the story in the correct order.
